title: Variables and Strings
description: Store values in variables and combine them with text.
objectives: Convert numbers to text with str()
recap: Variables hold values you name and reuse. The + operator glues strings together. str() turns a number into text so you can combine it with words.
nextLessonHint: In the next lesson, you'll ask the user a question and use what they type back.
practicePrompts: Create variables for a movie title and the year it came out, then print them on one line.
Try swapping two variables without using a third variable.

practiceExercises.title: Introduction line
practiceExercises.prompt: Create a variable `name = "Bob"` and a variable `age = 30`. Print one line in this exact form: `Bob is 30 years old.`
practiceExercises.goal: Use + and str() to combine a name and an age in one sentence.
practiceExercises.starterCode:
name = "Bob"
age = 30
# Print: Bob is 30 years old.
hints: Combine the pieces with +. age is a number, so use str(age) to make it text first.
Pattern: print(name + " is " + str(age) + " years old.")

practiceExercises.title: Swap two values
practiceExercises.prompt: Start with `a = 1` and `b = 2`. Swap the values so that `a` becomes 2 and `b` becomes 1, then print one line that says `a=2, b=1`.
practiceExercises.goal: Swap two variables and print the result.
practiceExercises.starterCode:
a = 1
b = 2
# Swap the values, then print: a=2, b=1
hints: Python lets you swap in one line: `a, b = b, a`.
Or use a temporary variable: tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp.
After swapping, build the output with +: print("a=" + str(a) + ", b=" + str(b))

practiceExercises.title: Profile card
practiceExercises.prompt:
Create variables `name = "Maya"` and `age = 22`. Print exactly two lines:
Name: Maya
Age: 22
practiceExercises.goal: Print a two-line card using two variables and string concatenation.
practiceExercises.starterCode:
name = "Maya"
age = 22
# Print Name: Maya on one line, Age: 22 on the next
hints: Use two print() calls — one for each line.
Second line: the age is a number; wrap it in str() before joining with +.
